title: Retain terminal-direct under matched shared pressure
question: Can a plain terminal-direct partition and probabilistic job preserve the completion and peer admission boundaries of the encoded snapshot path?
summary: At publication one fixed-peer pair completed direct only. At live emission a separate fixed request admitted alongside a completed snapshot job but was rejected by the direct job. Defer delivery.

workloads: 70,003 plain rows with four partition parents, internal seeded 80/20/0 allocations, one worker, strict row/byte caps, shared and job memory at 32 MiB.

validation.summary: 56 total complete-job attempts in the final primary and follow-up. Exact output and logical Analysis on success, one input visit, typed denial/cancellation, preserved late incumbent, and full owner/private staging cleanup. The primary Rust test passed and re-extraction recovered an omitted first log line.

limitations: Fixed callback-synchronized peer requests against a tracked shared ledger.
Variable pressure before or after these particular callbacks and other row widths, shapes and codec owners remain untested.
exclusions: No new timing, RSS, physical I/O, Windows/WASI validation, dispatch or default change.
reopen_when: Require a concrete live-writer admission remedy that preserves the matched peer completion without fallback after emission.
